summary: A heavy Luciani/Turczi euro about building railway and power-line networks across a steampunk map to deliver resources and unlock a deep tech tree. It plays like a fusion of Barrage-style engine optimization with network-building route games, offering several viable strategic paths.
praised: satisfying, interlocking tech-tree and action-retrieval systems
gorgeous board art and thematic production
criticised: heavy rules overhead and long teach time
significant analysis paralysis, especially at higher player counts
feels similar to other Luciani euros, which can fatigue fans of the genre

interaction.kind: claiming action cards before rivals and competing for shared network routes/resources
interaction.detail: The action-retrieval system means once you take a strong action card, opponents can't use that exact one until it cycles back, so timing to grab it first matters. The network board, coal/uranium market, and post rewards are shared and contestable, but each player still spends most of a turn developing their own rail lines and tech track.

scoring.how_you_win: You win by earning the most VP from expanding your rail/power network, completing delivery contracts, and climbing technology tracks before the building/track supply runs out and ends the game.
